headline: Constraints define boundaries—knowing what not to do is often more valuable than knowing what to do
universal_truth: Saying no creates focus; constraints enable rather than limit; boundaries define shape
fun_facts: Warren Buffett credits his success to the investments he didn't make, not the ones he did
Poets use constraints like meter and rhyme to force creativity
Software developers use 'not to do' lists to prevent feature bloat
discussion_questions: What should you stop doing to create space for what matters?
What constraints would actually help rather than limit you?
What's on your 'not to do' list?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Sculpture is removing what doesn't belong. Strategy is saying no to good options to focus on great ones. Knowing what not to do creates space for what to do. Constraints don't just limit—they define.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often focus on what to do, but knowing what not to do can be equally powerful. Why are constraints so valuable?

options.text: Constraints create focus and force creativity—by eliminating options, they channel energy toward what matters and push innovation within boundaries
options.response: Yes. Infinite options create paralysis. Constraints create clarity. When you can't do everything, you must choose what matters. Boundaries focus and channel energy.
They do prevent mistakes, but more powerfully, they enable focus and creativity...

q1.title: Subtractive Wisdom
q1.script: Addition is obvious; subtraction is wisdom. What you remove often matters more than what you add. Knowing what not to do clears space for what matters.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Subtractive Wisdom"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Forced Creativity
q2.script: Constraints force creativity. A sonnet must have 14 lines—the constraint creates the form. Limitations push innovation rather than preventing it.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Not-To-Do List
q3.script: A 'not to do' list might be more valuable than a 'to do' list. What will you actively avoid? What good opportunities will you decline to focus on great ones?
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Saying no creates focus. Constraints enable rather than limit. Define your boundaries deliberately.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 291. Tomorrow, we'll explore different ways of being smart—multiple intelligences. Until then, consider what you should stop doing.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Not-To-Do List - What Should You Stop?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify constraints and subtractions that create focus
growTrack.activity: Create a 'not to do' list. What activities, commitments, or habits should you eliminate? What good opportunities should you decline to focus on great ones? Define your boundaries.
